title: Unfair Trade Practice — Deposit Retention
text: A trade practice that adopts any unfair method or deceives a consumer, including a seller or service provider unreasonably withholding a refundable security deposit after the consumer has fulfilled the conditions for its return, is an unfair trade practice under this Act.

title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
text: A complaint may be filed by a consumer with the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission where the value of goods or services paid does not exceed one crore rupees. The complaint should include the facts of the dispute, the relief sought, and supporting documents such as receipts or agreements.

title: Security Deposit Limit
text: For residential premises, the landlord shall not collect a security deposit exceeding two months' rent. For non-residential premises, the deposit shall not exceed six months' rent.

title: Return of Security Deposit
text: The landlord shall return the security deposit to the tenant, after making due deductions for damages or unpaid dues, at the time of taking back vacant possession of the premises. If the landlord has NOT returned the deposit within one month of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant may approach the Rent Authority for recovery.

title: Deposit Returned Within Time
text: Where the landlord HAS returned the security deposit within the stipulated one-month period after due deductions, no further claim for delay shall lie against the landlord.

title: Time of Payment of Wages
text: Wages of an employed person shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day (for establishments with fewer than 1000 workers) or the tenth day (for larger establishments) after the last day of the wage period. Delay beyond this constitutes a violation.

title: Claims Arising Out of Deductions or Delay in Wages
text: An employee whose wages have been delayed or unlawfully deducted may file an application before the Authority appointed under this Act, ordinarily within 12 months of the date the wages became due, seeking payment along with compensation.

title: Who Can Access Free Legal Aid
text: Free legal aid is available to, among others, persons with an annual income below the limit prescribed by the respective State Legal Services Authority, women, children, persons with disabilities, and industrial workmen, for representation before courts and tribunals.
